Lessons.Title: Applying the Quadratic Formula (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: analyze and correct common errors in quadratic formula calculations, especially signed coefficients, discriminant order, numerator ±, and denominator2a; verify the roots by substitution. Original Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 18 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/18/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/18/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source emphasizes error analysis more than rote answer production.
Original equation 3x²−5x−2=0 has a3,b−5,c−2. Discriminant D=(−5)²−4×3×(−2)=25+24=49. Formula x=(5±√49)/6=(5±7)/6 yields x2 or−1/3. The factored form (3x+1)(x−2)=0 provides an independent check.

An incorrect student step might use −5 rather than +5 for −b, or divide numerator by3 instead of6. Both produce candidates failing original substitution. For the second equation 2x²+4x+5=0, discriminant16−40=−24, so no real roots; a correct error analysis must distinguish algebraic failure from simply choosing wrong ±.

Student task: annotate a deliberately incorrect worked solution, locate first invalid step, correct it using exact fractions, and check both roots. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for coefficient signs, discriminant, entire fraction evaluation and reasoned error diagnosis/verification.

KeyConcepts.Title: Signed coefficients
KeyConcepts.Definition: The minus sign in−b changes sign of b.

KeyConcepts.Title: Independent back-check
KeyConcepts.Definition: Plug roots into original or compare factors.

WorkedExamples.Title: Solve signed coefficients
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve3x²−5x−2=0.
WorkedExamples.Method: Preserve the solution set and verify each exact real root with the original quadratic equation.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find first sign mistake
WorkedExamples.Question: What if a student writes x=(−5±7)/6?
WorkedExamples.Method: Preserve the solution set and verify each exact real root with the original quadratic equation.
Steps: Test wrong candidate to show difference.

WorkedExamples.Title: Recognize no-real-root case
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve2x²+4x+5=0 over reals.
WorkedExamples.Method: Preserve the solution set and verify each exact real root with the original quadratic equation.
Steps: Negative discriminant means no real roots.
Do not use an ordinary real square root of−24.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Failing to negate a negative b
Treating no real roots as a calculator malfunction
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Negative D is a mathematical condition.

SummaryPoints: The quadratic formula requires precise handling of signs and grouping.
Negative discriminant yields no real roots.
